items.title: Satellite imagery analyzed by DniproOSINT shows the aftermath of recent Ukrainian strikes on Russia's drone base in Tsymbulova, Oryol region. The strikes reportedly hit UAV storage hangars and launchers for jet-powered Shaheds. Russia is expanding the site with 26 underground shelters for fuel and UAV warheads, plus small garages for unarmed drones. Numerous transport containers for Geran-5 jet drones are also visible near the launchers, some stored in the open. #Russia

Don't hit diesel fuel, because that's hurting the world." #Ukraine

items.title: Zelensky says Russia launched about 2,100 drones at Ukraine this week, many of them jet-powered Shaheds, along with nearly 1,700 guided bombs and 78 missiles. Near the Polish border in Volyn, he said a Russian drone strike burned a train locomotive and damaged a fuel station. #Ukraine

items.title: ❗️Poland's Operational Command says the threat during Russia's overnight attack on Ukraine was "real and close." Russian drones operated and struck targets just several to a dozen kilometers from Poland's border, prompting Polish military aircraft to deploy. Air raid sirens sounded in six districts, while border checks were temporarily suspended overnight. A drone reportedly hit a truck around 800 meters from the Dorohusk-Yahodyn border crossing. No violation of Polish airspace was recorded. #NATO

items.title: “It is so dangerous now in Slovyansk and Kramatorsk that police say it is time for civilians to get out. These neighbouring cities are the biggest still under full Ukrainian control in the eastern Donbas region. In the worst affected areas, forced evacuations of families with children have already begun, says Pavlo Dyachenko of Donetsk police. ‘This is the only way to save your life,’ he says, because security has deteriorated so much. ‘If you take Slovyansk, it used to be hit by glide bombs roughly once a week, but now it's almost every day…’ Over the summer, the number of civilians wounded by Russian attacks on the two cities increased from 70 in June to 212 in August, say Ukrainian police. Sixteen people died in June, 20 in July and 15 in August.” https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cwyz89w59l3o

items.title: Ukraine's Defense Forces struck two Russian oil refineries overnight on September 13: Slavyansk-EKO in Krasnodar region, where a fire was recorded, and TANECO in Nizhnekamsk, Tatarstan, where a tank caught fire. A Russian strike-drone storage, preparation and launch site in Millerovo was also hit. Ukraine's General Staff also confirmed that the September 11 strike on the Saratov refinery damaged an ELOU-AVT-6 primary oil processing unit and a section of main pipeline. #Russia

items.title: Third Army Corps commander Andriy Biletsky says Russia's military leadership has ordered the capture of Donetsk and Luhansk regions by mid-April, while Russia's political leadership is demanding it before the start of 2027. Biletsky says Ukrainian forces have every chance to hold favorable defensive lines and the so-called fortress-city belt. He also expects clear improvements on some sectors of the Donetsk front within the next month. #Ukraine

items.title: Azov commander Denys Prokopenko warns Russia could use mobilization reserves this winter along Ukraine's northern border to try to create a buffer zone in Sumy and Chernihiv regions, forcing Ukraine to divert reserves from other fronts. He also expects Russia to shift tactics as weather worsens, moving from small infantry groups toward heavier armor and mechanized breakthroughs. Prokopenko says such pressure could also support continued Russian attacks on Kyiv. #Ukraine

items.title: ❗️Ukraine is bracing for a difficult winter as intensified Russian attacks hit infrastructure, industry and Black Sea exports. Economy Minister Oleksandr Kravchenko estimates nearly $10 billion in infrastructure and fixed-asset damage this year, with the broader economic toll equal to about 1.5 percentage points of GDP. Around $40 billion in export revenue is at risk, while the daily cost of the war has risen to about $190 million from $140 million in 2024. #Ukraine

items.title: "Russia’s oil-processing is being degraded as sanctions prevent the refining industry from recovering from more intense and precise Ukrainian drone strikes, according to the International Energy Agency. 'It now appears likely that the persistent drone strikes and the patchwork nature of repairs are having a cumulative negative effect and degrading the refining system,' the Paris-based agency said in a monthly oil report published Friday. Ukraine has been attacking Russia’s energy infrastructure to reduce the nation’s ability to process and export crude and curtail the Kremlin’s revenues used to finance the full-scale invasion. In August, the Russian oil refineries were hit at least 22 times, the highest monthly total since the start of the war, according to a Bloomberg tally based on public statements from both nations. The IEA revised down its baseline outlook for Russian oil processing over the next 18 months to around 4 million barrels a day, down 30% from levels before the invasion of Ukraine, it said." https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-11/ukraine-strikes-degrade-russian-oil-refining-industry-iea-says

items.title: Ukraine's Cabinet of Ministers plans to establish a special fund to insure businesses against war-related risks, although funding it may require a 1-percentage-point increase in value-added tax (VAT). Oleksandr Kravchenko: 'According to our estimates, business losses from attacks could reach US$10 billion this year. That's an unprecedented scale. We understand that the programmes we currently have – the loss compensation programme, and the 5-7-9% preferential lending scheme – can't meet the needs of all businesses. They work for small and medium companies, but don't cover the needs of large businesses.' To address this, the government is proposing to establish an insurance fund to compensate businesses for the first US$10 million in losses from a Russian attack." https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2026/09/12/8053083/

items.title: “Deep in Arctic waters near the remote Svalbard archipelago this spring, NATO allies caught Russian subs training to unleash a secret weapon designed to disable critical undersea cables without leaving any fingerprints. The clandestine Russian operation, described to Reuters by two Western officials, was carried out by Moscow's GUGI undersea warfare directorate, which used deep-sea submersibles to simulate the deployment of the sophisticated and destructive technology. A joint operation involving Britain, Norway and the United States tracked and confronted the Russian vessels at sea, said the two officials, speaking on condition of anonymity. The vessels were prevented from completing their exercise and eventually left the area.” https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/nato-allies-foil-russian-subsea-cable-sabotage-plot-2026-09-10/

items.title: RT by @RALee85: 1/ EXCLUSIVE: at @RFERL we obtained photos of a Russian flotilla in Tartus port, taken early September. This is the 1st instance in months of a Russian military ship being docked there, month after the announcement that Russia’s bases in Syria would be 'transferred' to Damascus.
items.summary:
1/ EXCLUSIVE: at @RFERL we obtained photos of a Russian flotilla in Tartus port, taken early September. This is the 1st instance in months of a Russian military ship being docked there, month after the announcement that Russia’s bases in Syria would be 'transferred' to Damascus.
GeoInsider (@InsiderGeo)
UPDATE: 🇷🇺🇸🇾 After around two months of absence, Russia is back in the Mediterranean, with a Russian naval convoy now arriving at Tartus, Syria.
Our team at @SONARROW_OSINT has been tracking the convoy since August 25. The four Russian vessels have travelled from the Atlantic into the Mediterranean and across the region before reaching the Syrian coast.
The SPARTA Ro-Ro cargo ship and AKADEMIK PASHIN replenishment oiler are now docked at Tartus. The SPARTA appears to have already unloaded its cargo.
The ADMIRAL LEVCHENKO Udaloy-class destroyer and GENERAL SKOBELEV tanker are not currently inside the port. They may be operating offshore, similar to how the ADMIRAL FLOTA KASATONOV has operated around Tartus in recent months.
What exactly was delivered to Tartus remains unclear, but the return of a Russian convoy to the Syrian port after months away is significant.
So the key questions remain: What did SPARTA bring to Syria, and how long will the Russian vessels remain at Tartus?
— https://nitter.netbub.com/InsiderGeo/status/2098012800320749673#m

The ADMIRAL LEVCHENKO Udaloy-class destroyer and GENERAL SKOBELEV tanker are not currently inside the port. They may be operating offshore, similar to how the ADMIRAL FLOTA KASATONOV has operated around Tartus in recent months.
What exactly was delivered to Tartus remains unclear, but the return of a Russian convoy to the Syrian port after months away is significant.
So the key questions remain: What did SPARTA bring to Syria, and how long will the Russian vessels remain at Tartus?
